instructions: The day before, or up to 3 days ahead: melt 8 tbsp of the butter and let it cool until it's only warm. In a large bowl, whisk the melted butter with 1 cup warm water (about 110°F), the sugar, the salt and the yeast.
Add 5 of the eggs and whisk until smooth.
Add 5 1/2 cups of the flour all at once and stir with a wooden spoon until no dry flour is left. The dough will be wet and lumpy. That's right.
Cover the bowl loosely, not airtight, and leave it at room temperature for 2 hours.
Refrigerate the dough for at least 3 hours, or up to 3 days.
On baking day, use the last 1 tbsp of butter to grease two loaf pans, each about 8 1/2 by 4 1/2 inches.
Flour the counter with a little of the extra 1/2 cup of flour. Cut the cold dough in half and put one half back in the fridge.
Knead the half on the counter for about 30 seconds, adding a little flour if it sticks. Cut it into 3 equal pieces and roll each into a rope about 13 inches long.
Pinch the 3 ropes together at one end, braid them, and tuck the ends under. Transfer the braid into one of the pans.
Take the second half out of the fridge and shape and braid it the same way, then put it in the other pan.
Cover the pans loosely and leave them at room temperature for 90 minutes, until puffy.
While they rise, heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle.
Beat the last egg and brush it over both loaves.

Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until deep golden brown. You're baking it to about 190°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Tap the bottom of a loaf. It should sound hollow.
Cool the loaves in their pans on a rack for 15 minutes. Turn them out and cool completely before slicing.
Keep one loaf wrapped in a bag or foil at room temperature, where it keeps for a few days. Slice the other loaf, wrap it well and freeze it for up to 2 months. Thaw slices at room temperature.
advance_prep_notes: Make the dough 3 hours to 3 days ahead; it needs 2 hours at room temperature, then 3 hours in the fridge.
method_notes: Once Upon a Chef (the lead, 4.96 from 22 ratings) is a no knead dough that is stirred together, rested 2 hours, then chilled for up to 3 days before it is shaped and baked, which is how it fits a weekend bake. Pinch and Swirl chills a smaller tangzhong dough for 12 to 24 hours and shapes it as a rolled loaf; it agrees on 350°F and a golden top at about 190°F inside. The lead makes two loaves, so one goes in the freezer. Prep time counts the rising and chilling, since the dough has to be made ahead.
